messages.content:
Here is the trip. It is everything you get.

Shape: road-trip
Leaving from: Montréal, Québec
Going to: Gaspésie
Dates: 2027-07-03 to 2027-07-11, fixed
Travellers: 4
Ages that change the plan: 41, 39, 11, 7
Access needs: not answered
Budget: 4200 CAD, total
Appetite for effort: moderate
Roughest night they will accept: simple
Would rule the trip out: No more than one night in any campground without showers

About this road-trip:
How much road a day holds: half-day
Vehicle: car
Whose vehicle: own
Route style: loop
Stops they already want: Percé Rock, Forillon National Park
In their words: The seven-year-old is miserable after about three hours in the car, so we would rather stop often than push through. We have done the north shore before and would like to see something new.

candidatesAccepted.summary: A stop the party already wants, and a short, easy one that suits frequent breaks for the seven-year-old. candidatesAccepted.title: Forillon National Park coastal walks
candidatesAccepted.summary: Named by the party as a stop they want, and its coastal headlands and beaches can be taken in short, separate stretches that fit the wish to stop often. I have not checked trail lengths, seasonal opening, or fees, and access needs were not answered, so I cannot say which paths suit the youngest travellers.

candidatesAccepted.title: Bonaventure Island seabird boat trip
candidatesAccepted.summary: A new experience that is not on the north shore, with a gannet colony viewed from the water. Boat schedules, crossing time, weather dependence, and season are all unchecked, and access needs were not answered, so the suitability for a seven-year-old and the timing are unknown.

candidatesAccepted.title: Seafood lunch at a Percé waterfront shack
candidatesAccepted.summary: A casual seafood stop suits a mixed-age group and a child who tires in the car, and regional fish is a real part of the Gaspésie food scene. Access needs were not answered, so I could not check seating or step-free entry, and I have not confirmed this venue's opening days. These details come from general knowledge, not the map data, which covers only Montréal and Québec City.

candidatesAccepted.title: Smoked fish and bakery picnic from a Gaspé market
candidatesAccepted.summary: Buying smoked fish and fresh bread for a picnic lets the party eat when the child needs a break from the car, and it fits a moderate effort level. Access needs were not answered, so I could not check whether the spot has accessible parking or seating, and I have not verified its hours. These details come from general knowledge, not the map data.

candidatesAccepted.title: Bonaventure Island boat trip from Percé
candidatesAccepted.summary: A boat crossing to the seabird colony on Bonaventure Island, with Percé Rock in view, is a good stop for the family. The cost band assumes adult fares for all four travellers because children's fares are unknown to me, so the true figure may be lower. Access needs are not answered, so I cannot say whether the boarding and island walking suit everyone.

candidatesAccepted.title: Percé Rock viewing from the town beach
candidatesAccepted.summary: Stopping at the shoreline to see Percé Rock costs little and can be done in short bursts, which suits a seven-year-old who tires in the car. Low-effort and easy to leave at any point. I did not check beach access or parking, and access needs are not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: Forillon National Park coastal trails
candidatesAccepted.summary: Short coastal trails in Forillon offer something new compared with the north shore and let the children stretch between stops. The cost band covers a park entry fee for your own car, but I have not confirmed current park fees or whether a pass is needed. Access needs are not answered, so trail suitability is unknown.
